question: Does the HTTP fingerprint substrate discriminate when response bodies and status codes are identical but server-side state changes only independent header fields (Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie, Vary) — isolating header-only drift from the vacuous body/status confound where full==body==status==1.0 and C4 is degenerate?
hypothesis: The HTTP fingerprint substrate (hash of status + body_bytes + sorted filtered standard headers, excluding Date/Server/X-Request-Id) will discriminately detect header-only server-state changes: when the server returns byte-identical bodies and identical 200 status codes but differs only on independent headers (Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie, Vary) via a writable server-side state change, full-vector discrimination will be >0.5 (expected 1.0 deterministic) and B-HEADERS-ONLY will be >0.5, while B-STATUS-ONLY and B-BODY-ONLY will be 0.0, making full-vector > max(status,body) — the first non-vacuous C4 test. The null control (same header state resampled) will remain 0.0 (CI containing 0.0, upper bound <=0.05), demonstrating no false positive when headers are stable. Content-Length will be identical across conditions, proving header discrimination is not body-correlated.
falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if, on verified header-only drift comparisons where status codes are identical (200 vs 200) and response bodies are byte-identical (SHA-256 equal, Content-Length identical): (a) full-vector discrimination <=0.5, OR (b) B-HEADERS-ONLY discrimination <=0.5, OR (c) B-STATUS-ONLY !=0.0 or B-BODY-ONLY !=0.0 (indicating body/status confound not isolated), OR (d) full-vector fails to strictly exceed max(B-STATUS-ONLY, B-BODY-ONLY), OR (e) null control (same header state, two independent samples of N=20) discrimination >0.05 or CI does not contain 0.0. Any single failure triggers FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING for header-only drift. Infrastructure failure (server crash, header-set write not committed, fingerprint computation error) yields MEASUREMENT_INVALID, not falsification.

baselines.description: Fingerprint = status code only. Expected 0.0 on all header-only drift comparisons because status is 200 vs 200. Strong null that proves body/status confound is isolated; if this baseline is >0, the experiment is not header-only.

Fingerprint = response body SHA-256 only (exact bytes). Expected 0.0 on all header-only drift comparisons because bodies are byte-identical. Strong null; Content-Length identical verifies no body-correlation. Demonstrates that body alone cannot detect header drift.

Fingerprint = sorted filtered standard headers only (Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie, Vary, Content-Type, Content-Length, Connection) excluding Date/Server/X-Request-Id. Expected >0.5 (ideally 1.0) on header-only drift comparisons. Positive baseline showing header signal is independently discriminative; full-vector should track this baseline when body/status are constant.

positive_control: Header-only drift via writable server-side header_config (SQLite or in-memory dict committed via POST /admin/set_headers, verified by SQLite SELECT before observation). Primary comparison: STATE_A (baseline) = GET /resource with headers Cache-Control: max-age=3600, ETag: W/"aaa-111", Vary: Accept-Encoding, no Set-Cookie  vs  STATE_E (combined drift) = same endpoint with headers Cache-Control: max-age=0, must-revalidate, ETag: W/"bbb-222", Vary: Accept-Encoding, Origin, Set-Cookie: session=hdrdrift; Path=/; HttpOnly  — bodies both 200 + {"data":"hello","version":1} byte-identical (SHA-256 equal, Content-Length identical). Per-header isolations also measured: A vs B (Cache-Control only change), A vs C (ETag only), A vs D (Set-Cookie only). Full-vector and B-HEADERS-ONLY must each achieve discrimination >0.5 on A-vs-E and on at least 2/3 per-header isolations. Setup verified by: (1) SQLite header_config committed before observation batch; (2) status 200 on all observations; (3) body SHA-256 equality check across A vs E; (4) raw observed headers show expected header values per state.
null_control: Same-state resampling: two independent batches of N=20 GET /resource observations from the same header state (STATE_A sampled twice with 50-150ms jitter, no server write between batches). Expected full-vector discrimination =0.0 (both batches produce identical fingerprints; all 20 fingerprints within each batch byte-identical, set size 1). Bootstrap 95% CI must contain 0.0 with point estimate <=0.05. Also verifies B-STATUS-ONLY and B-BODY-ONLY remain 0.0 on null. A second null (STATE_E resampled) reported as exploratory. This tests false-positive rate when headers are stable — distinct from parent's fresh vs near-expiry null which tested identical-code-path token metadata; this null tests header stability.
measurement_validity: Server state snapshot: header_config (Cache-Control, ETag, Vary, Set-Cookie) read from SQLite/in-memory store and logged before each observation batch to confirm intended state; POST /admin/set_headers commit verified by subsequent SELECT
Status identity verified: all observations in header-only comparisons must be status=200; any non-200 aborts the comparison as measurement failure

Body byte-identity verified: SHA-256(body_bytes) must be identical across STATE_A/B/C/D/E; Content-Length header must be identical across states (proving header discrimination not via body-correlated Content-Length)

Header inclusion/exclusion: Date, Server, X-Request-Id excluded from fingerprint exactly as parent (EXCLUDED_HEADERS same set); Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie, Vary INCLUDED and logged raw; any missing expected header is a validity failure

Fingerprint computation: hash(status + body_bytes + sorted_filtered_headers) identical algorithm to parent (research/experiments/EXP-RUNTIME-35697043449/run_experiment.py:compute_fingerprint); code path hashed and stored in provenance

Seed and jitter: SEED=44 deterministic, jitter 50-150ms uniform between observations same as parent for reproducibility; N=20 per state (5 states x20 =100 plus 40 null-control lines =140 raw lines expected, but effective distinct N reported)

Degenerate CI disclosure: with deterministic responses fingerprints within a state are byte-identical (expected set size 1 per state); bootstrap CI will be degenerate [1.0,1.0] or [0.0,0.0] and is reported as deterministic, not as inferential precision; effective distinct N=1 reported alongside nominal N=20

Server freshness: Flask dev server started fresh per run on 127.0.0.1 with free port (discoverable, default 19848), no residual header_config; port and Flask/PyJWT/SQLite versions recorded in provenance

Timing: header_config write committed (SQLite WAL COMMIT or dict update) before next observation batch; sequential request-response, no concurrent load (concurrency explicitly out of scope and listed in unresolved)
Artifact integrity: run_experiment.py, raw_observations.jsonl, experiment_result.json SHA-256 logged in provenance; recomputation of Jaccard distances by auditor must match producer
product_consequence_positive: C-MEAS-VALID advances within EXPERIMENTAL with ceiling expanded to include header-only drift: substrate discriminates independent header changes (Cache-Control/ETag/Set-Cookie/Vary) when bodies and statuses are identical, closing audit V2 (ceiling effect) and V3 (header correlation) and providing the first non-vacuous C4 (full > body/status). This unblocks C-FRESHNESS (freshness guards can detect metadata/cache drift without body change) and C-DELTA-REPAIR (perturbation measurement when only metadata varies) for localhost synthetic testing. Does NOT promote to VALIDATED or PRODUCT_CORE: still bounded to Flask dev server localhost, no production WSGI/nginx, no CDN, no concurrent load, no distribution, and per-header signal strength remains to be characterized for header freshness policies.
product_consequence_negative: C-MEAS-VALID remains EXPERIMENTAL with header-only drift falsified: HTTP fingerprint substrate (status+body+filtered headers) cannot discriminate server-side header-only state changes when bodies and status are identical, or can only do so via Content-Length correlation (which will be caught by C6). This means the current header selection / hashing / filtering (or Flask dev server header handling) is insufficient for header-only drift detection. C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR cases where response content is unchanged but metadata varies (cache headers, ETag, cookies) remain unmeasurable with this substrate; alternative substrates (browser-DOM observation, explicit header-aware comparison, or production-grade header handling) are required. Distributed/production testing remains blocked. Negative result still closes the vacuous-C4 gap by demonstrating the boundary of the substrate.
estimated_cost: Low: single Flask server + SQLite/in-memory dict on localhost, no external dependencies beyond Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT (already installed), N=140 observations (5 states x20 + 2 null batches x20), ~5-7 min execution, deterministic; no Docker, no nginx, no CDN.
expected_information_gain: High and discriminating: first experiment to break the 40-streak vacuous C4 (full==body==status==1.0) by isolating header-only drift. Positive outcome expands C-MEAS-VALID ceiling to the header-only condition that is the actual C-FRESHNESS/C-DELTA-REPAIR use case (session/auth drift when content unchanged) and provides the verified nginx HIT/SWR/SIE substrate's missing complement (those tests validated body-identical oracle-free decompression; this validates header-identical-but-metadata-different discrimination). Negative outcome is equally decisive: it falsifies header-only detection with current fingerprint and forces a substrate redesign, preventing wasted distributed testing on a non-discriminating measurement. Either outcome changes the product decision about whether header freshness is measurable on localhost before scaling to production.
